name: ערך מוחלט וארגומנט ראשי של מספר מרוכב (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if b=0 then abs(a) else igcd2(b,mod(a,b))

functions.name: texp
functions.body: if constantp(x) and freeof(%i,x) and is(x<0) then sconcat("\\left(",tex1(x),"\\right)") else tex1(x)

functions.name: texnsum
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], sconcat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], if constantp(t) and is(t<0) then sconcat("-",tex1(-t)) else sconcat("+",tex1(t))), rest(L)))))

functions.name: rsq
functions.body: block([s,t,nn,dd,aa:1,mm:1,g,u], if ratnump(x) then return(tex1(x)), s: if is(x<0) then "-" else "", t: ratsimp(x^2), nn: num(t), dd: denom(t), for f in ifactors(nn*dd) do (aa: aa*f[1]^floor(f[2]/2), mm: mm*f[1]^mod(f[2],2)), g: igcd2(aa,dd), aa: aa/g, dd: dd/g, u: sconcat(if aa=1 then "" else string(aa), "\\sqrt{", string(mm), "}"), if dd=1 then sconcat(s,u) else sconcat(s,"\\frac{",u,"}{",string(dd),"}"))

functions.name: cxq
functions.body: block([r1:"", i1:""], if p#0 then r1: rsq(p), if q#0 then (i1: if is(abs(q)=1) then "\\mathrm{i}" else sconcat(rsq(abs(q)), "\\mathrm{i}"), i1: if is(q<0) then sconcat("-",i1) else if p#0 then sconcat("+",i1) else i1), if p=0 and q=0 then "0" else sconcat(r1,i1))

questiontext:
Consider the complex number

\[ z={{CT:0}} \]

Evaluate the modulus of \(z\) \((r = |z|)\) and the principal value of the argument of \(z\) (\(\theta = \mathrm{Arg}(z)\)). Enter your results in the correct order, i.e. \([r,\theta]\).

\([r,\theta] = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: The modulus is \(r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are the real and imaginary parts. For the argument, the reference angle comes from \(\tan\alpha=|y/x|\), and the quadrant of \(z\) (the signs of \(x\) and \(y\)) gives the principal value in \((-\pi,\pi]\).
Step 1 — The modulus
Write \(z=x+iy\), with real part \(x={{CT:1}}\)[[if test="{{CT:14}}"]] \(={{CT:2}}\)[[/if]] and imaginary part \(y={{CT:3}}\)[[if test="{{CT:15}}"]] \(={{CT:4}}\)[[/if]]. The modulus is the distance of \(z\) from the origin:

\[ r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=\sqrt{\left({{CT:1}}\right)^2+\left({{CT:3}}\right)^2}=\sqrt{{{CT:5}}+{{CT:6}}}=\sqrt{{{CT:7}}}={{CT:8}} \]

Step 2 — The argument
The tangent of the argument is

\[ \tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}={{CT:9}} \]

but the tangent alone does not determine \(\theta\): angles that differ by \(\pi\) have the same tangent. So first find the reference angle \(\alpha\), the acute angle between the segment from the origin to \(z\) and the real axis:

\[ \tan\alpha=\left|\frac{y}{x}\right|={{CT:10}}\ \Rightarrow\ \alpha={{CT:11}} \]

Then the signs of \(x\) and \(y\) give the quadrant. The principal value \(\mathrm{Arg}(z)\) is the argument in the interval \(-\pi\lt\theta\le\pi\). [[if test="{{CT:16}}"]]Here \(x>0\) and \(y>0\), so \(z\) lies in the first quadrant and the argument equals the reference angle:

\[ \theta=\alpha={{CT:12}} \]

[[/if]][[if test="{{CT:17}}"]]Here \(x\lt 0\) and \(y>0\), so \(z\) lies in the second quadrant:

\[ \theta=\pi-\alpha=\pi-{{CT:11}}={{CT:12}} \]

[[/if]][[if test="{{CT:18}}"]]Here \(x\lt 0\) and \(y\lt 0\), so \(z\) lies in the third quadrant. The angle \(\pi+\alpha\) points to \(z\), but it is larger than \(\pi\); the principal value is obtained by subtracting \(2\pi\):

\[ \theta=-\pi+\alpha=-\pi+{{CT:11}}={{CT:12}} \]

[[/if]][[if test="{{CT:19}}"]]Here \(x>0\) and \(y\lt 0\), so \(z\) lies in the fourth quadrant, below the positive real axis:

\[ \theta=-\alpha={{CT:12}} \]

[[/if]]Check: \({{CT:8}}\cos\left({{CT:13}}\right)={{CT:1}}\) and \({{CT:8}}\sin\left({{CT:13}}\right)={{CT:3}}\).
Step 3 — The answer
In the requested order:

\[ [r,\theta]=\left[{{CT:8}},\ {{CT:12}}\right] \]
